transcript: Last night, I saw Dakar 2000 by Rajiv Joseph at MTC. This is a new play with two characters in Senegal at the turn of the millennium. It starts with them meeting under rather unassuming circumstances, but evolves into somewhat of a political spy thriller. I didn't find either character very likable, but I did find them interesting, and their backstories and context are seamlessly folded into the plot, leading to an extremely efficient 80 minutes. I think this efficiency is what makes this a great play — it keeps you on the edge of your seat, with every scene bringing a new type of tension or intrigue. So even if you're feeling a little room-temperature about the premise like I was, I think you'll still find this to be an impressive display of acting, direction, and writing. With that, another playbill for my collection.
